deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 117 continues a German prose summary of ancient Macedonian history, probably notes from a history lecture or a textbook (in the style of Heeren's Göttingen history teaching). The hand looks like a careful, school-like Kurrent with Latin script for proper names. It may not be Gauss's own; it could be a family member's or a student's exercise bound into the bundle. The previous page covers the early kings, submission to Darius Hystaspis, and Amyntas I and Alexander I. This page continues as follows. (1) In 479 BC, after the Persian defeat, the Macedonians recovered and became independent but soon faced new difficulties. Athens had colonies on the coast. Disputes arose under Perdiccas II, given in the margin as reigning 454–413. (2) The Thracians became very powerful at this time. In 423 Perdiccas made peace with Athens and so secured his position. (3) Archelaus followed (margin 413–400). He made Macedonia a kingdom ('Reich'), built military roads and fortified places, and left an under-age son, Orestes. (4) Orestes was murdered by his guardian Aeropus (margin 400–394). Aeropus was himself murdered in 394. (5) Amyntas II (modern numbering: Amyntas III) took the throne, dated 390–369. The war with Olynthus, 'a republic', falls in his reign. He left 3 sons, all of whom reigned. The next page gives a genealogy (Alexander, Perdiccas, Philipp; Amyntas, Alexander M.) and Pelopidas' interventions. There are no derivations, formulas, or computations to reconstruct.
errors: Historical, not mathematical: Archelaus' reign is usually dated 413–399 BC, not 413–400.
Historical, not mathematical: the king the manuscript calls 'Amyntas II' is now called Amyntas III. He is usually dated 393–370 BC, versus the manuscript's 390–369.
Historical, not mathematical: Aeropus II is usually dated c. 398/7–395/4 BC. The manuscript's 400–394 interval is roughly consistent with the older chronology.
The sentence 'Athen hatte Kolonien an der Küste, und machte sich nun auch unabhängig' is awkwardly compressed. The subject of 'machte sich unabhängig' is ambiguous as written.
deep.surprise_reason: The page holds only elementary notes on ancient Macedonian history, with no mathematical content. Possibly it is not even in Gauss's hand. Nothing here bears on the history of mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Line 14: 'der Krieg mit Olynth einen[?] Augenblick[?]' should almost certainly read 'der Krieg mit Olynth, einer Republik'. The image shows '...mit Olynth [ein]er Republik.', and Olynthus/the Chalcidian League was a republic.
Line 4: 'Streitigkeiten' is plausible. It is written split as 'Streitig keiten', followed by 'un=' carried over to 'ter Perdiccas II'.
The marginal 'regierte 454 – 413.' belongs to Perdiccas II. The margin dates '413 – 400' belong to Archelaus and '400 – 394' to Orestes/Aeropus.
'Archelaus' and 'Aeropus' are written in Latin script, distinct from the surrounding Kurrent.
